<STRUCT_0001>
The following lemma is the analogue of
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0001>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
Let <MATH_0002> be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0003>
which is smooth local on source-and-target. Let <MATH_0004> be a morphism
of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0005>. The following are equivalent:
<STRUCT_0001>
<ITEMOPEN_0001>(a)<ITEMCLOSE_0001> <MATH_0006> has property <MATH_0007>,
<ITEMOPEN_0002>(b)<ITEMCLOSE_0002> for every <MATH_0008> there exists a smooth morphism of pairs
<MATH_0009>, a smooth morphism <MATH_0010>, and
a morphism <MATH_0011> such that <MATH_0012> and
<MATH_0013> has <MATH_0014>,
<ITEMOPEN_0003>(c)<ITEMCLOSE_0003> for some commutative diagram
<MATH_0015>
with <MATH_0016>, <MATH_0017> smooth and <MATH_0018> surjective the morphism <MATH_0019> has <MATH_0020>,
<ITEMOPEN_0004>(d)<ITEMCLOSE_0004> for any commutative diagram
<MATH_0021>
with <MATH_0022> smooth and <MATH_0023> smooth
the morphism <MATH_0024> has <MATH_0025>,
<ITEMOPEN_0005>(e)<ITEMCLOSE_0005> there exists a smooth covering <MATH_0026> such
that each base change <MATH_0027> has <MATH_0028>,
<ITEMOPEN_0006>(f)<ITEMCLOSE_0006> there exists a smooth covering <MATH_0029> such
that each composition <MATH_0030> has <MATH_0031>,
<ITEMOPEN_0007>(g)<ITEMCLOSE_0007> there exists a smooth covering <MATH_0032> and
for each <MATH_0033> a smooth covering
<MATH_0034> such that each morphism
<MATH_0035> has <MATH_0036>.
<STRUCT_0002>

The equivalence of (a) and (b) is part of
Definition <REF_0001>.
The equivalence of (a) and (e) is
Lemma <REF_0002> part (2).
The equivalence of (a) and (f) is
Lemma <REF_0003> part (1).
As (a) is now equivalent to (e) and (f) it follows that
(a) equivalent to (g).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
It is clear that (c) implies (b). If (b) holds, then for any
<MATH_0001> we can choose a smooth morphism of pairs
<MATH_0002>, a smooth morphism <MATH_0003>, and
a morphism <MATH_0004> such that <MATH_0005> and
<MATH_0006> has <MATH_0007>. Then <MATH_0008>
with <MATH_0009> and <MATH_0010> is a diagram as in (c).
(Note that <MATH_0011> has property <MATH_0012> as <MATH_0013>
is a smooth covering and <MATH_0014> is smooth local on the target.)
Thus (b) is equivalent to (c).

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Now we know that (a), (b), (c), (e), (f), and (g) are equivalent.
Suppose (a) holds. Let <MATH_0015> be as in (d). Then
<MATH_0016> has <MATH_0017> as <MATH_0018> is stable under
smooth base change, whence <MATH_0019> has <MATH_0020> as <MATH_0021>
is stable under precomposing with smooth morphisms. Conversely, if (d)
holds, then setting <MATH_0022> and <MATH_0023> we see that <MATH_0024> has <MATH_0025>.
